I've been playing Albion Online recently and can't get enough of it. It's very simple, you only have a few spells at your disposal but complexity comes into the PVP combat when you are against another team of different weapons with different abilities that you must figure out how to counter. Positioning is also very important in PVP. PVE is a little less focused on but there are still dungeons and the standard tank, heals, dps, strategy is at play here. There's also many other aspects to the game as well: Farming is really peaceful and allows you to provide resources to your guild or just to sell and make money, Gathering is really addictive because you go out and find good resources but you have be on your toes so as to not get ganked in the red and black zones, crafting is fun and a great way to amass tons of in-game money if you can get your hands on the resources to do it, and you can even build up your personal island and a guild island. Later on if you are a hardcore player and you manage to get into a guild you'll end up getting into GVG fights. these are 5v5 arena fights for territories on the game map. Owning territories gives a guild access to farmland, better gathering spots, their own little villages to build and live in and can be a huge advantage for gearing out their players. Even if you are not a hardcore player there are guilds that want farmers or crafters or gatherers and in any of those roles you get to take advantage of whatever territories your guildies win so it's win-win and it's really fun. There are of course PVE guilds too and the developers have stated that PVE will be getting fleshed out and more polished in the future because there was a ton of interest in it.

The game is currently in open beta but the devs have hinted at a release sometime around august. No definitive date yet though. There will be wipes before the game is released.

As for monetization they originally stated that the game would eventually become free to play but have since backtracked on that, i think partially because of input from the community. As it stands now there is an upfront fee to get an account and then you can play forever, however there is a standard account and premium account status, premium account gives you more gathering, more skill unlocks and basically gives you a time-advantage, with premium you won't have to spend quite as long grinding to get to a certain gear level, but you will still have to grind. Basically almost everyone in the game is on premium because you can obtain premium with in-game silver or gold. so as long as you play regularly it's not too difficult to maintain premium status indefinitely, but if you go on hiatus and come back or you want to use in-game currency for other stuff you can buy in-game gold with real money and use that to buy premium. It's a bit complicated but it's not really pay to win in the end, more like grind or pay to remain competitive, but once you're in that arena it's all skill.

It might not be worth getting into right now because there will be wipes coming soon but it's worth keeping an eye on.
